checks.s: The proposed limitation-of-liability cap is stated as a specific dollar amount or formula that does not exceed $5,000,000.
The proposed limitation-of-liability cap is at least $3,630,000.
The proposed limitation-of-liability cap is no greater than $5,000,000.
The limitation-of-liability compromise states a specific dollar figure or a clear percentage formula for the cap.
The deliverable shows an arithmetic derivation of the limitation-of-liability cap from the SOW #4 fee figures, such as a percentage of the $7,260,000 total SOW fee or $7,260,000 ÷ 1.5 = $4,840,000.
The proposed acceptance-testing period is specifically stated as longer than 10 business days and shorter than 45 calendar days.

The acceptance-testing clause provides a middle-ground deemed-acceptance mechanism, such as deemed acceptance after a defined period with a structured rejection or cure process, rather than automatic acceptance on silence alone or affirmative sign-off only.
The liquidated-damages clause calculates damages using the $1,210,000 per-milestone payment amount rather than the $7,260,000 total SOW value.
The liquidated-damages clause sets an aggregate cap on total liquidated damages payable for any single milestone.
The rationale explains why uncapped liquidated damages would be disproportionate.
The rationale discusses cumulative liquidated-damages exposure across delay-duration scenarios, such as 1-week, 4-week, 8-week, or 12-week delays.
The IP clause expressly identifies PredictaCore™ Engine as Verdantis pre-existing IP that is not assigned or transferred to Crestline.
The IP clause references Copyright Registration TX-9-214-558.
The IP clause treats pre-existing IP as a distinct category retained by Verdantis and licensed to Crestline.
The IP clause treats custom algorithms or deliverables created specifically for Crestline under SOW #4 as a distinct category.

The IP clause proposes an intermediate ownership or licensing structure for those custom algorithms or deliverables, rather than full Verdantis retention with a narrow license or full work-for-hire assignment to Crestline.
The IP clause addresses derivative works or improvements to pre-existing IP as a distinct category and specifies their ownership or licensing treatment.
The limitation-of-liability rationale explicitly states that the proposed cap falls within the playbook's walk-away parameters.
The limitation-of-liability rationale explains how the proposed cap complies with the playbook's walk-away parameters.

The deliverable addresses limitation of liability, acceptance testing, liquidated damages, and IP ownership.

Each of the four contested terms—limitation of liability, acceptance testing, liquidated damages, and IP ownership—includes proposed compromise language drafted as contract-ready clauses rather than only bullet points or summaries.
Each of the four contested terms includes a supporting negotiation rationale explaining why the compromise is commercially reasonable.
Each of the four contested terms includes a supporting negotiation rationale explaining how the compromise addresses Crestline's concerns and protects Verdantis's core interests.
The compromise liquidated-damages rate is greater than 0.5% of per-milestone value per week.
The liquidated-damages rate is applied to the $1,210,000 per-milestone payment amount, not the $7,260,000 total SOW value.
The liquidated-damages rationale explains why calculating damages on the $1,210,000 per-milestone basis is more proportionate than calculating them on the $7,260,000 total SOW value.
The limitation-of-liability rationale references the MSA default cap of 100% of fees paid in the 12 months preceding the claim and its approximate $4,840,000 run-rate value.
The limitation-of-liability rationale references Verdantis's $5,000,000 E&O per-occurrence limit.
The limitation-of-liability rationale identifies Verdantis's SOW #4 position as $3,630,000, or 50% of SOW fees.
The limitation-of-liability rationale identifies Crestline's SOW #4 position as $14,520,000, or 200% of SOW fees.
The limitation-of-liability rationale references the SOW #3 precedent cap of 100% of SOW #3 fees and explains how the SOW #4 compromise departs from or tracks that precedent.
The acceptance-testing rationale references the SOW #3 precedent of 20 business days with deemed acceptance and explains how the SOW #4 compromise relates to it.
The liquidated-damages rationale references the SOW #3 service-credit precedent of 0.5% per week capped at 10% per milestone and explains how the SOW #4 compromise departs from or tracks it.
The IP rationale references the SOW #3 precedent of Verdantis retaining IP with a license to Crestline and explains how the SOW #4 compromise relates to it.
The IP clause grants Crestline a license to PredictaCore™-based pre-existing IP that is perpetual, non-exclusive, royalty-free, and for internal use.
The IP clause explicitly states whether the pre-existing IP license is limited to Plant 1/Breckton, Plant 2/Tremaine, and Plant 3/Whetstone or extends to additional Crestline facilities.

The proposed compromise clauses use defined terms consistent with the MSA and SOW drafts, such as 'Service Provider,' 'Customer,' 'Deliverable,' 'Milestone,' 'SOW Fees,' 'Pre-Existing IP,' or 'Custom Deliverables,' or substantially equivalent terms.
The acceptance-testing rationale addresses Crestline's argument that plant-floor integration complexity and production-cycle validation require longer testing windows.
The acceptance-testing rationale explains how the proposed period balances Crestline's need for adequate testing against Verdantis's interest in avoiding payment delays caused by extended testing.
The limitation-of-liability clause includes or addresses a mutual exclusion of consequential, indirect, and/or punitive damages.
The limitation-of-liability rationale notes that the E&O policy excludes consequential and punitive damages and explains how the contractual exclusion aligns with insurance coverage.
The deliverable references the August 15, 2025 board-imposed execution deadline.
The deliverable references the July 28, 2025 internal review deadline.
The negotiation rationale uses both parties' mutual time pressure, including their work toward the same deadlines, as a reason supporting compromise.
The compromise liquidated-damages clause uses the term 'liquidated damages,' rather than referring only to 'service credits.'
The liquidated-damages clause states that the liquidated-damages amount is a genuine pre-estimate of loss.
The liquidated-damages clause states that actual damages would be difficult to ascertain.
The stated limitation-of-liability cap dollar amount is arithmetically correct when the stated percentage or formula is applied to the $7,260,000 total SOW #4 fixed fee.
The acceptance-testing compromise retains a deemed-acceptance mechanism.
The acceptance-testing clause requires written notice before the deemed-acceptance clock starts.
The acceptance-testing clause requires Verdantis to provide a detailed test report with each deliverable submission.
